saints.name: St. Colette
saints.title: Virgin, Reformer of the Poor Clares
saints.shortBlurb: A carpenter's daughter who restored the Poor Clares to their original poverty and founded a strict reform of the order…
biography: Born Nicolette Boellet at Corbie in Picardy on 13 January 1381, the daughter of a carpenter of the abbey, Colette was left an orphan at eighteen. After trying the Beguines and a Benedictine house, she took the habit of the Third Order of St. Francis in 1402 and lived four years as a recluse beside the abbey church.

Convinced by visions that she was called to restore the Poor Clares to their first poverty, she went in 1406 to Peter de Luna, acknowledged in France as Pope Benedict XIII, who received her at Nice, gave her the veil of the Second Order, and by a series of bulls empowered her to found and reform monasteries.

Beginning at Besançon in 1410, she founded or reformed eighteen monasteries in her lifetime, prescribing absolute poverty, bare feet, and perpetual abstinence; those of her obedience were called Colettines. In this work she was aided by her confessor, the Franciscan Henry de Beaume.

She died at Ghent on 6 March 1447, worn out by penance and travel, and her body rests in the church of her monastery there. Canonized by Pope Pius VII in 1807, she is invoked by childless couples and by expectant mothers.
saints.knownFor: The reform of the Poor Clares (the Colettines).

sources.text: Butler, Lives of the Saints (1866 ed.), 6 March
